implementation.name: original-v1-fairness-threshold
implementation.scope: Original 16-applicant toy drawing; counts of drawn markers only. A shared boundary, then a Subgroup B-specific cutoff shown with its FPR cost and legal caveat. Not the LoanFairness credit-service metrics; no score values or recommended remedy.
implementation.question: Where do the errors go when the boundary moves?

purpose: Move one shared approval boundary from the 75% candidate line left to the 81.25% candidate line, one marker at a time, and watch each subgroup's misclassifications change: every gain falls in Subgroup A while Subgroup B's denied repayers go from one to three. A sweep of all 17 shared positions confirms 81.25% is the unique best shared accuracy (every other position at most 75%), yet B's TPR is 0.25 against A's 1.00. Then Subgroup B gets its own, more lenient cutoff: it recovers B's repayers and equalizes TPR at 1.00, at the cost of approving a B defaulter (FPR 0.25 vs 0.00), the threshold-adjustment trade-off described after the figure.
storyboard: Establish the two rows, the sixteen toy applicants, and both candidate lines with nothing applied. State the score direction once: further left is a higher score, so a boundary approves to its left and moving it right is more lenient.
Apply the 75% boundary (right-hand line) to both rows: approvals only (A 7 of 8, B 3 of 8), outcomes not yet checked.
Check decisions against outcomes: A 3 approved defaulters, B 1 denied repayer; 12 of 16 correct (75%).
Move 1 (left, stricter): deny a B repayer; A 3, B 2; 68.75%.
Move 2: deny an A defaulter; A 2, B 2; 75%.
Move 3: deny another B repayer; A 2, B 3; 68.75%.
Move 4: deny another A defaulter; A 1, B 3; 75%.
Reach the 81.25% line: A 0, B 3 (all denied repayers); 13 of 16 correct.
Compare the candidates and sweep every shared position, shown as a per-position strip: 81.25% only here, all 16 others at most 75%; B TPR 0.25 vs A 1.00.
Give B its own cutoff (A stays): B regains its two middle repayers; B 1 error (a denied repayer), TPR 0.75, FPR 0.00; overall already 93.75%, above every shared boundary, with no false positive.
B's cutoff approves a defaulter: B 2 errors, FPR 0.25, TPR still 0.75, accuracy 87.5%; equal TPR cannot be reached without passing this defaulter.

B's cutoff approves its last repayer: TPR 1.00 equals A's, FPR 0.25 vs A's 0.00; B's one error is now an approved defaulter; 15 of 16 overall, the same as B cutoff 1, so the false positive is the price of equal TPR; legal caveat and 'a policy decision, not a metric'.
guard: Marker positions, boundaries, colors, shapes, and the approve-left rule come from the TikZ source exactly (commit ce4d703324 positions); error marking uses a dashed ring and a cross glyph, not color. Intermediate stops sit between drawn markers and display no score value; dashed labels remain accuracies. The shared phase moves in the caption's direction (75% to 81.25%). The split phase is labeled as no longer one shared boundary, keeps A fixed on the 81.25% line, states the FPR cost and the prose's legal caveat, and does not present the 93.75% toy accuracy as a recommendation. No LoanFairness numbers.
